fields.value: Machines as a first-class model: allocation to runs, costs, and load metrics

Design Etude's model of machines and what runs on them, then deliver a first milestone that includes the table stake: CPU, memory and GPU charts for a run without the training code asking for them.

## Why

Weights & Biases shows machine metrics for every run by default; Etude records none, and Manabot samples RSS and host load by hand in its training loop. The charts are one feature of a bigger change in how Etude thinks about machines.

## Direction

Jack Heart, 2026-11-13:

"For machine metrics I think there's a bigger change that I want: a slight reframe around the way that we think about machine management. Just making sure that we think about it this way: you have a set of machines that are running and those have a mapping to the tasks that they're allocated. There may be some sort of budget or costs associated with those tasks, training runs, or experiments.

I'm not exactly sure on the right mapping, maybe both. I think probably a run has an experiment tied to it. You tie the runs to the machines and then inherently that ties the experiments and machines.

I want there to be global views and also I want there to be things like, 'Oh this experiment ran, bought this machine to run this test.' Honestly it doesn't need all of it and you can reuse some of it. If somebody else wants to do it, 'Oh I see that. Rather than renting a new machine I can just hop onto this other machine.'

I think we want to make sure that the core notion of machines is well established. With that obviously you should be able to see graphs of how loaded all of your machines are, and machine metrics for every machine. I assume that we want to build that system.

We also want that to be tied to this: on any given experiment you see the graphs for your machines that that experiment, or that run, is running on. If your run is not the only thing on that machine, if your experiment is not the only thing on that machine, you both kind of want to know: 'Okay what is the load that my process is generating versus what is the total load on the machine?' We might need to differentiate that."

And on scope: "these both deserve their own tasks, but they are bigger than just that. lets frame the task as design the bigger system, make progress towards it, make sure first milestone includes these tablestakes".

## Outcome

1. A design for the machine model:
   * A machine is a lasting thing with a record of which runs it is allocated to; a run belongs to an experiment, so experiments and machines are tied through runs. Settle whether any direct experiment-to-machine tie is also needed ("maybe both" is open).
   * Costs and budgets: what a machine cost, which run or experiment it was rented for, and how the cost is attributed when it is shared.
   * Reuse: seeing that a rented machine has spare capacity and putting another run on it, including someone else's.
   * Global views: every machine and its load. Per-run and per-experiment views: the machines that run or experiment is on.
   * Two measures kept apart: the load this run's processes generate and the total load on the machine.
2. A first milestone, built: CPU, memory and GPU metrics recorded per machine and shown on each run, with the run's own share distinguishable from the machine's total, with no call from training code.

## Constraints

* Sampling must not load the machine or slow training; no artificial load in tests.
* Works for owned SSH hosts, rented machines and this computer.
* The sibling Task on the live view owns where runs are viewed and whether a server exists; this Task owns machines and metrics. Their designs must agree on what a run page shows.

## Context

Comparison and positioning notes: `scratch/explore.html` and `scratch/positioning.md` in the Manabot worktree `manabot.aa55a0-move-run-execution` (MTG-329). Existing pieces: `Allocation` and providers (`src/etude/launch/machines.py`), pools and "Several runs on one machine" (`docs/launcher.md`), attempt records with host and pod (`src/etude/train/run.py`), transfer usage (`src/etude/launch/usage.py`). Manabot's hand-rolled sampling is `resource_metrics` in `manabot/training/loops/self_play.py` on the MTG-329 branch.
